answer.rationale: Primary contract ends in 14 days with no auto-renew and the line is at 94% with no buffer, so deferral or a primary switch would raise delivery risk and is incompatible with the TCO-without-more-risk objective. Prior cycles indicate incumbent renewal preserved integration and deliveries (c1) and that renewal-point benchmarking plus multi-year volume terms cut unit cost without shrinking scope (c4, c6). The single decision this cycle is therefore a full-volume terms negotiation with the incumbent aimed at the 18% spend cut, not a source change. Verifying c4 because it is unknown whether prior renegotiation recovered anything close to 18%. c2 onboarding speed, c3 second-source, and c5 month-to-month deferral (non-critical service) are not treated as established for this cliff. Negotiation failure still threatens continuity, so downstream value risk is flagged.
